Luke saw this as a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity and eagerly accepted.

Upon boarding the ship, Luke learned that it would be carrying 335 horses along with their supplies. The entire crew took turns caring for the animals, while nightwatchmen ensured their safety throughout the night. One particularly rainy evening, Luke was assigned the night watch. After completing his hourly report to the captain, he slipped down a slippery ladder and tumbled onto his back. Terrified, he felt himself hurtling towards an opening on the side of the ship before a small piece of metal stopped his fall. Though relieved to have survived, Luke was unable to work for several days due to cracked ribs.

Turning 18 during a stop in Greece, Luke faced the possibility of being drafted into military service. However, when his draft board discovered his current assignment, they advised him to continue his travels. Some of Luke's most memorable moments were during the return voyage, when the ship had dropped off its cargo and the crew could enjoy the vast open spaces they had been exploring.

Reflecting on his experiences, Luke was grateful for the opportunity to embark on such an adventure. This journey truly broadened his horizons and deepened his understanding of the world.
